origin.reason: English rendering of the router-core design template, with status notes where a step is not implemented yet. A request is routed to READ, PLAN, RUN, AUDIT, SYNC, PROJECT, UPDATE, WORK or LEADER through references/routes.json; an open question is sorted before anyone is asked; a report figure names its command (an empty output is not zero); and the skill asks the host's agent tool for delegation.

Written for SPEC-20261122-next-flow-skills-agents (REQ-6, REQ-7, text slice B; decisions D-4, D-5, D-6): the one audit contract, at most 6144 bytes. What the auditor receives, what it returns, which session records the verdict (a card note read by the lander) and that the author of a change never audits it, with five side rules: a local code review of the base..head range without its fix or comment options, a re-audit to the first auditor, a lane's tree-bound check receipt, no forked or advisor session, and a finding without file and line counts as none. It absorbs the former internal review note, whose two security sentences keep their pins (tests/core_rules_2876.rs), and points to RUN's check-run rules instead of restating them. Named by the AUDIT row of chains/index.md and by the moai-audit agent's body.

Moved out of the SYNC workflow by the RUN and SYNC procedure SPEC: the lander and release part (effects, landing, release pull request, CI evidence, independent review, release merge, reconcile, integration receipt). Named once by SYNC.

Written for SPEC-20261122-next-flow-skills-agents (REQ-5, text slice B; decisions D-2, D-8, D-9): the one full description of the flow, at most 6144 bytes. It explains the name once, describes the four technical rules as how the flow runs, and states the worktree place, that a lane submits its head and base only, the landing command, the protection hook, the fast-forward push only when the user has turned the remote copy on, and that remote checks never block a landing. Each landing and hook statement was checked against src/card/land.rs and src/card/guard.rs. The flow rule file in the config folder points here (REQ-11).

Written for SPEC-20261125-agent-team-session-names (REQ-19 to REQ-22, decision D-5): the message table of the leader window and the agents (dispatch, question, answer, audit request, verdict, repair request, landing notice, completion, next card), the notice rule, the agent-to-agent rule, the address rule and the channel order. It lives in its own file so the flow reference stays within its byte budget.

Written for SPEC-20261122-claude-md-flow-rule revision 4 against the leader's candidate (rules-redesign-2026-11-23): the short, project-generic evidence and handoff rule that moai-cli writes as rules/moai-flow.md into each Claude config folder the user picks (src/home_routing/rules.rs), plain text with no frontmatter, at most 80 lines and 5 KiB. Lane, card and landing detail stays in references/flows/next-flow.md, which this file points to; what hooks enforce (force push, reset, clean) is not repeated here.

Moved out of the RUN workflow by the RUN and SYNC procedure SPEC: heavy slots, one build folder per worktree, cleanup and the build cache facts, with the Python slot and tool paths removed. Read from RUN step 1.

Written for SPEC-20261126-change-claims-and-test-guard (REQ-9): how to list the claims of a change and match each to the diff, the four labels, how to check deleted or altered tests and the tests that read an altered output, and the repair ready note. Read by moai-impl and moai-audit through their reads: lists.

Moved out of the RUN workflow by the RUN and SYNC procedure SPEC: who runs which check, when a remote run may be cited, the test rules and the flaky rule, with internal numbers, tool paths and Python lines removed. Read from RUN step 5.

Written for SPEC-20261120-destructive-ops-checklists (user instruction 2026-11-20, a survey of the skills and agents against that day's audit findings): the checks for code that removes, moves or overwrites data the user owns (a link in any path component, NUL-separated machine output, commits that stay reachable, the way back saved first, a just-created target left alone, a nested repository left alone, failing closed). The `reads:` lines of moai-audit and moai-impl that name it come with a later SPEC.

Written for SPEC-20261123-skill-structure from the user-confirmed skill structure (2026-11-21): an internal reference read only before a session arms a timer that repeats the leader round; it defines the confirmed leader by the session registry (src/leader_round/registration.rs) and allows one timer, so the skill entry only points to it.

How a question reaches the user in UPDATE and PROJECT: the session runs the commands itself, every question is a selection with the recommended option first, and one table names the question tool per host with its plain-text fallback. Named by update.md, project.md, internal/interview and the PROJECT row of chains/index.md instead of being repeated.

The checks whoever wrote a change runs before asking for an audit or opening a pull request, one line each with its command, grouped as tests, package and documents, and the pull request. Read by moai-impl (`reads:`) and named by the rules of chains/index.md; its machine items are run by the repository's own check script.

Moved out of the RUN workflow by the RUN and SYNC procedure SPEC: the change-specific rules, the shell and helper rules and the host worktree guard table, with internal numbers removed. Read from RUN Exceptions and Permissions.
Moved out of the RUN workflow by the RUN and SYNC procedure SPEC: how a session reads a web page. Read from RUN step 2.

English rendering of the router-core design template, with status notes where a step is not implemented yet. The routes are READ, PLAN, RUN, AUDIT, SYNC, PROJECT, UPDATE, WORK and LEADER; the top-level `chains` names references/chains/index.md, the agent order per route.

Written for SPEC-20261124-moai-leader-route (REQ-1 to REQ-12): `/moai leader` makes the window that types it the registered coordination window; it registers with `session-register`, renews once per round, reads the ledger, sends audits to another session, lands with `moai card land --by leader` and releases the registration at the end. The completion-message and transition sentences stay in `flows/next-flow`.
